From cd1635d844d26471c56c0a432abdee12fc9ad735 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yu Kuai <yukuai@fnnas.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Jan 2026 02:26:22 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] md/raid5: fix IO hang with degraded array with llbitmap

When llbitmap bit state is still unwritten, any new write should force
rcw, as bitmap_ops->blocks_synced() is checked in handle_stripe_dirtying().
However, later the same check is missing in need_this_block(), causing
stripe to deadloop during handling because handle_stripe() will decide
to go to handle_stripe_fill(), meanwhile need_this_block() always return
0 and nothing is handled.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-raid/20260123182623.3718551-2-yukuai@fnnas.com
Fixes: 5ab829f1971d ("md/md-llbitmap: introduce new lockless bitmap")
Signed-off-by: Yu Kuai <yukuai@fnnas.com>
Reviewed-by: Li Nan <linan122@huawei.com>

diff --git a/drivers/md/raid5.c b/drivers/md/raid5.c
index 6d408aaaacf3..8854e024f311 100644
--- a/drivers/md/raid5.c
+++ b/drivers/md/raid5.c
@@ -3751,9 +3751,14 @@ static int need_this_block(struct stripe_head *sh, struct stripe_head_state *s,
 	struct r5dev *dev = &sh->dev[disk_idx];
 	struct r5dev *fdev[2] = { &sh->dev[s->failed_num[0]],
 				  &sh->dev[s->failed_num[1]] };
+	struct mddev *mddev = sh->raid_conf->mddev;
+	bool force_rcw = false;
 	int i;
-	bool force_rcw = (sh->raid_conf->rmw_level == PARITY_DISABLE_RMW);
 
+	if (sh->raid_conf->rmw_level == PARITY_DISABLE_RMW ||
+	    (mddev->bitmap_ops && mddev->bitmap_ops->blocks_synced &&
+	     !mddev->bitmap_ops->blocks_synced(mddev, sh->sector)))
+		force_rcw = true;
 
 	if (test_bit(R5_LOCKED, &dev->flags) ||
 	    test_bit(R5_UPTODATE, &dev->flags))
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes an IO hang in the `md/raid5` driver that occurs with a degraded array when using the lockless bitmap (llbitmap). The root cause is an inconsistency in checks for bitmap block synchronization between two critical code paths.

### Modifications in each file:

- **drivers/md/raid5.c**  
  In the `need_this_block()` function, the condition for setting `force_rcw` (force reconstruct write) is extended. Previously, `force_rcw` was only set to `true` when `rmw_level == PARITY_DISABLE_RMW`. Now it also becomes `true` if the bitmap operations indicate that the blocks for the stripe are not yet synced (`mddev->bitmap_ops->blocks_synced()` returns `false`).  
  The added code is:
  ```c
  if (sh->raid_conf->rmw_level == PARITY_DISABLE_RMW ||
      (mddev->bitmap_ops && mddev->bitmap_ops->blocks_synced &&
       !mddev->bitmap_ops->blocks_synced(mddev, sh->sector)))
      force_rcw = true;
  ```

### Relationship between modifications:

The bug occurred because two functions that decide whether a block operation should be handled now or must wait for the bitmap ensure consistency:  
- `handle_stripe_dirtying()` already checks `blocks_synced()` to force RCW when the bitmap is unwritten.  
- `need_this_block()` lacked this same check, leading to a deadlock loop: `handle_stripe()` could opt for `handle_stripe_fill()`, but `need_this_block()` would return 0 (incorrectly skipping the block), causing nothing to progress.  

By adding the bitmap sync check to `need_this_block()`, the fix aligns the two decision points, ensuring that new writes are consistently forced into the RCW path when the bitmap state is still unwritten, thereby preventing the hang.

Here is the commit message:
md/raid5: fix IO hang with degraded array with llbitmap

When llbitmap bit state is still unwritten, any new write should force
rcw, as bitmap_ops->blocks_synced() is checked in handle_stripe_dirtying().
However, later the same check is missing in need_this_block(), causing
stripe to deadloop during handling because handle_stripe() will decide
to go to handle_stripe_fill(), meanwhile need_this_block() always return
0 and nothing is handled.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-raid/20260123182623.3718551-2-yukuai@fnnas.com
Fixes: 5ab829f1971d ("md/md-llbitmap: introduce new lockless bitmap")
Signed-off-by: Yu Kuai <yukuai@fnnas.com>
Reviewed-by: Li Nan <linan122@huawei.com>

Here is the root cause:
In the need_this_block() function, the condition for forcing RCW (reconstruct write) only checked for PARITY_DISABLE_RMW, but did not check whether the llbitmap blocks are synced via mddev->bitmap_ops->blocks_synced(). Meanwhile, handle_stripe_dirtying() already had this check. This inconsistency caused handle_stripe() to repeatedly choose handle_stripe_fill() while need_this_block() always returned 0, leading to a deadloop and IO hang with degraded arrays using llbitmap.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int need_this_block(struct stripe_head *sh, struct stripe_head_state *s,
 			   int disk_idx, int disks)
 {
 	struct r5dev *dev = &sh->dev[disk_idx];
 	struct r5dev *fdev[2] = { &sh->dev[s->failed_num[0]],
 				  &sh->dev[s->failed_num[1]] };
+	struct mddev *mddev = sh->raid_conf->mddev;
+	bool force_rcw = false;
 	int i;
-	bool force_rcw = (sh->raid_conf->rmw_level == PARITY_DISABLE_RMW);
 
+	if (sh->raid_conf->rmw_level == PARITY_DISABLE_RMW ||
+	    (mddev->bitmap_ops && mddev->bitmap_ops->blocks_synced &&
+	     !mddev->bitmap_ops->blocks_synced(mddev, sh->sector)))
+		force_rcw = true;
 
 	if (test_bit(R5_LOCKED, &dev->flags) ||
 	    test_bit(R5_UPTODATE, &dev->flags))
 		/* No point reading this as we already have it or have
 		 * decided to get it.
 		 */
 		return 0;
 
 	if (dev->toread ||
 	    (dev->towrite && !test_bit(R5_OVERWRITE, &dev->flags)))
 		/* We need this block to directly satisfy a request */
 		return 1;
 
 	if (s->syncing || s->expanding ||
 	    (s->replacing && want_replace(sh, disk_idx)))
 		/* When syncing, or expanding we read everything.
 		 * When replacing, we need the replaced block.
 		 */
 		return 1;
 
 	if ((s->failed >= 1 && fdev[0]->toread) ||
 	    (s->failed >= 2 && fdev[1]->toread))
 		/* If we want to read from a failed device, then
 		 * we need to actually read every other device.
 		 */
 		return 1;
 
 	/* Sometimes neither read-modify-write nor reconstruct-write
 	 * cycles can work.  In those cases we read every block we
 	 * can.  Then the parity-update is certain to have enough to
 	 * work with.
 	 * This can only be a problem when we need to write something,
 	 * and some device has failed.  If either of those tests
 	 * fail we need look no further.
 	 */
 	if (!s->failed || !s->to_write)
 		return 0;
 
 	if (test_bit(R5_Insync, &dev->flags) &&
 	    !test_bit(STRIPE_PREREAD_ACTIVE, &sh->state))
 		/* Pre-reads at not permitted until after short delay
 		 * to gather multiple requests.  However if this
 		 * device is no Insync, the block could only be computed
 		 * and there is no need to delay that.
 		 */
 		return 0;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < s->failed && i < 2; i++) {
 		if (fdev[i]->towrite &&
 		    !test_bit(R5_UPTODATE, &fdev[i]->flags) &&
 		    !test_bit(R5_OVERWRITE, &fdev[i]->flags))
 			/* If we have a partial write to a failed
 			 * device, then we will need to reconstruct
 			 * the content of that device, so all other
 			 * devices must be read.
 			 */
 			return 1;
 
 		if (s->failed >= 2 &&
 		    (fdev[i]->towrite ||
 		     s->failed_num[i] == sh->pd_idx ||
 		     s->failed_num[i] == sh->qd_idx) &&
 		    !test_bit(R5_UPTODATE, &fdev[i]->flags))
 			/* In max degraded raid6, If the failed disk is P, Q,
 			 * or we want to read the failed disk, we need to do
 			 * reconstruct-write.
 			 */
 			force_rcw = true;
 	}
 
 	/* If we are forced to do a reconstruct-write, because parity
 	 * cannot be trusted and we are currently recovering it, there
 	 * is extra need to be careful.
 	 * If one of the devices that we would need to read, because
 	 * it is not being overwritten (and maybe not written at all)
 	 * is missing/faulty, then we need to read everything we can.
 	 */
 	if (!force_rcw &&
 	    sh->sector < sh->raid_conf->mddev->resync_offset)
 		/* reconstruct-write isn't being forced */
 		return 0;
 	for (i = 0; i < s->failed && i < 2; i++) {
 		if (s->failed_num[i] != sh->pd_idx &&
 		    s->failed_num[i] != sh->qd_idx &&
 		    !test_bit(R5_UPTODATE, &fdev[i]->flags) &&
 		    !test_bit(R5_OVERWRITE, &fdev[i]->flags))
 			return 1;
 	}
 
 	return 0;
 }

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (sh->raid_conf->rmw_level == PARITY_DISABLE_RMW ||
    (mddev->bitmap_ops && mddev->bitmap_ops->blocks_synced &&
     !mddev->bitmap_ops->blocks_synced(mddev, sh->sector)))
    force_rcw = true;
Reason:
This replaces the simple assignment with a conditional that sets force_rcw to true if either RMW is disabled or the llbitmap blocks are not yet synced (i.e., blocks_synced returns false). By replicating the same condition used in handle_stripe_dirtying(), it ensures that need_this_block() correctly forces a reconstruct-write (RCW) when the bitmap indicates unwritten blocks. This prevents the deadloop because now the stripe will be handled via handle_stripe_dirtying() instead of repeatedly attempting handle_stripe_fill() with need_this_block() returning 0.
